uncited: Recursive Octree Traversal is a depth-first algorithm for processing a 3D sparse voxel octree by visiting every node in the tree structure.

It differs from its siblings by explicitly using the call stack to manage recursion depth, whereas [Iterative Octree Traversal](2618-iterative-octree-traversal.md) uses an explicit stack, and [Parametric Octree Traversal](2361-parametric-octree-traversal.md) uses parametric ray-marching logic.
The method consists of two primary phases: tree construction (optional, depending on the source) and recursive traversal.
The traversal visits nodes to either render them as geometry or process them for mesh generation.
Recursive octree traversal is a fundamental algorithm in computer graphics, originating from early 3D modeling and ray-tracing systems.
It is widely used in voxel-based editors, Marching Cubes implementations, and sparse voxel octree renderers.
